description: SandboxPilot (github.com/LeanBytes/SandboxPilot) screenshot plan for MacPacker. MacPacker's launch parameters (-ArchivePath / -NavigatePath / -SearchQuery / -SelectItem / -NewArchive) are a general feature — a way to open an archive and jump to a file inside it from the command line, a script, or automation, not tied to any screenshot tool. This file is simply the first consumer: it tells a screenshot driver which parameters, scenarios and appearances produce MacPacker's localized screenshots. -DisableUpdateChecks, -ExtractDemo and -DropZone are automation/preview flags used only for the shots. The archives the scenarios name are generated by assets/screenshots/make_demo_archives.py into ~/Downloads/MacPacker-Demo (too big to commit, and the only place the sandbox can read without a file picker); a debug build resolves them from there by file name. Scenarios are numbered to match the media-kit frames they feed — FrameBison composes background, pointers and dragged files on top, since a drag itself cannot be simulated, which is what -DropZone stands in for. Quick Look and Finder integration are deliberately absent: both run in other processes (the QuickLook host, Finder) that SandboxPilot cannot drive or capture.

scenarios.name: 01-browse
scenarios.description: Archive browser — the handoff archive open at its root, one file selected

scenarios.name: 02-nested
scenarios.description: Browsing nested archives — navigated into an archive inside the archive, a file in it selected

scenarios.name: 03-edit
scenarios.description: Creating and editing ZIP archives — an existing zip with a file added to it and not yet saved, so the window reads 'Edited'

scenarios.name: 04-search
scenarios.description: Searching inside an archive — the toolbar filter showing matches from every level at once

scenarios.name: 05-new-archive
scenarios.description: Creating a new archive — a fresh archive filled with files and not yet saved (empty would show nothing at all)

scenarios.name: 06-extract-selection
scenarios.description: Selective extraction — two files selected, ready to be dragged out (FrameBison adds the pointer and the dragged file)

scenarios.name: 07-drop-add
scenarios.description: Drag & drop — the drop-zone overlay pinned with the 'add' zone highlighted (FrameBison adds the pointer and the dragged file)

scenarios.name: 08-extraction-progress
scenarios.description: Extraction progress window at 1/3 of a large file, details expanded so the speed chart is visible (uses the -ExtractDemo preview flag)
